---
title: "Assess and filter sampling compliance"
output: html_document
---

Compliance is calculated during conversion from registered targets and observed
sampling times. Filtering creates a separate analysis-ready object without
changing the complete evidence-bearing results.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(carwatch)

study_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "carwatch-gallery-compliance")
generate_synthetic_study_data(
  study_dir,
  n_participants = 4,
  non_compliant_sample_ratio = 0.20,
  missing_awakening_time_ratio = 0,
  missing_sampling_time_ratio = 0,
  random_state = 42,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

folders <- list.dirs(file.path(study_dir, "logs"), recursive = FALSE, full.names = TRUE)
participant_dirs <- stats::setNames(folders, basename(folders))
raw_logs <- read_raw_logs_from_participant_dirs(participant_dirs)
study_results <- convert_raw_logs(raw_logs, errors = "raise")
```

```{r assess}
summarize_compliance(study_results)
find_non_compliant_samples(study_results)
find_sampling_anomalies(study_results)
```

By default, one failed sample clears its entire canonical day in the analysis
copy. Registration, scheduling, and source provenance remain present.

```{r filter}
analysis_results <- drop_non_compliant_samples(study_results)

nrow(as_sample_events(study_results))
nrow(as_sample_events(analysis_results))
summarize_compliance(analysis_results)
```

```{r plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
plot_compliance_overview(study_results, view = "heatmap")
```
